newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate dips at close on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate dips at close on liquidity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 70 basis points at 22.00 percent on Monday due to a late surge in liquidity, traders said.
"From the start we were very nervous and kept a close eye on the sliding peso, for which reason trading was confined to covering shorts," a dealer said.
"Nonetheless, some money flowed in towards the close, maybe from traders who preferred to wait, but overnight rates will go back up to 22.50 percent tomorrow," he added.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed up 60 basis points at 24.10 percent.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts earlier closed 4.9 centavos weaker at 7.9875/7.9950 per dollar, but managed to rein in an initial plunge to 8.03/8.05 per dollar.
Traders said the volatile peso fueled forecasts of increases in primary rates at Tuesday's central bank auction. Bellwether 28-day Cetes were expected to gain by more than 300 basis points.
"Although there were almost no trades in term instruments, bids are pointing towards considerable increases, particulalry at 28 days," a trader said.
Bids of 22 percent were tendered for 28-day paper in the secondary market, compared to last week's auction rate of 18.59 percent.
The central bank drained 523 million pesos from the market through two auctions, which it assigned at 23.94 and 24.08 percent.
Liquidity of 334 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Tuesday.
